u0: The shop is running with no unmet obligation currently active: the siren is silent, and no client order, food preparation, or immediate food recovery is pending. The task is not complete, because the episode continues and future clients or siren rings will create new work. The agent can reposition or wait and react when the next scheduled event occurs.
u1: The siren has started ringing and has not been switched off. The remaining requirement is to reach the siren switch and toggle it. Other shop work can be done meanwhile, but the siren will not stop on its own.
u10: Prepared food has just slipped out of the agent's hands. The next step must pick it up so the agent is holding food again; otherwise the mandatory immediate recovery is violated. Once recovered, the prepared food still needs to be served to the waiting client.
u11: Prepared food has just slipped while the siren is ringing. The next step must restore the food to the agent's hands, or the immediate pickup rule is broken. After that, the prepared food still needs to be served, and the siren still needs to be switched off.
u12: A client has arrived and is waiting at the counter. The order has not yet been taken, so the agent must take it, get food ready at the stove, and serve the client. The client remains until served.
u13: A client has arrived and is waiting, while the siren is ringing. The order has not been taken yet, so the client still needs an order taken, food prepared, and service. Separately, the siren must be switched off; both obligations remain until handled.
u14: A client is waiting and prepared food is ready for them; preparation implies the order has already been taken. The remaining step is to serve that prepared food to the client. The client stays until the food is handed over.
u15: A client is waiting with prepared food ready, and the siren is ringing. The prepared food still needs to be served, and the siren must be switched off. Both jobs remain outstanding until the corresponding actions happen.
u16: A client has arrived and the food has just slipped. The next step must recover the food so it is held again, or the hard immediate-pickup rule fails. The client's order has not yet been taken; after recovering the food, the agent must take the order, prepare food, and serve the client.
u17: A client is waiting, the siren is ringing, and the food has just slipped. The very next step must recover the food; missing that would break the immediate-pickup rule. After recovery, the client's order still must be taken, prepared, and served, and the siren must be switched off.
u18: A client is waiting and prepared food has just slipped from the agent's hands. The next step must restore the food to hand; otherwise the mandatory immediate pickup is missed. After recovery, the prepared food still needs to be served to the client.
u19: A client is waiting with prepared food that has just slipped, and the siren is ringing. The next step must recover the food, or the immediate-pickup requirement fails. After that, the prepared food must be served and the siren switched off.
u2: A client's order has been taken, and that client is waiting to be served. The order still needs food prepared at the stove, after which the prepared food must be handed to the client. The task remains in progress until that service is completed.
u20: An order has already been taken but not yet prepared, and a client is waiting whose order has not yet been taken. The agent still needs to prepare and serve the outstanding order and to take the waiting client's order. Both remain open requirements; reaching this state does not satisfy either.
u21: An order is still waiting to be prepared, and a client is waiting to give their order. The siren is ringing, so its switch must eventually be toggled off. Those shop duties can continue while the siren is handled, but the taken order, the waiting client, and the ringing siren all remain unfinished.
u22: An order has been taken without being prepared, a client is waiting to order, and food has just slipped from the agent's hands. The fallen food must be picked up on the very next step; if it is not, the task fails irreversibly. Recovering the food leaves the outstanding order and the waiting client still to be handled.
u23: An order still needs preparation, a client is waiting to give their order, and the siren is ringing. Food has also just slipped from the agent's hands and must be picked up on the next step, or the task fails immediately. After that pickup, the siren switch, the taken order, and the waiting client all remain outstanding.
u24: Prepared food is still waiting to be served, and an order has been taken whose food has not yet been prepared. The agent must serve the prepared portion and prepare and serve the taken order. Neither requirement is finished.
u25: Prepared food still needs to be served, and a taken order still needs preparation. The siren is ringing, so a toggle at its switch is also owed. The agent can silence the siren while working through the food obligations, but all three requirements remain unresolved.
u26: A prepared portion is waiting to be served, a taken order is awaiting preparation, and food has just slipped from the agent's hands. The slip must be recovered on the very next step; a missed pickup is an irreversible failure. Once recovered, the prepared-food service and the order preparation still remain.
u27: Prepared food awaits serving, a taken order awaits preparation, and the siren is ringing. Food has just slipped as well, so the agent must pick it up on the next step or fail permanently. After that immediate pickup, the siren and the two outstanding food obligations still need attention.
u28: A required next-step pickup was missed after food fell, so a mandatory requirement has been violated for good. The failure is irreversible: the shop task can no longer be completed, whatever the agent does afterward.
u29: Prepared food is still waiting to be served, a taken order has not been prepared, and a client is waiting to have their order taken. The agent must serve the prepared portion, prepare and serve the taken order, and take the waiting client's order. All three are outstanding; reaching this state completes none of them.
u3: A client's order has been taken while the siren is ringing. The waiting order still needs food prepared and served, and the siren must be switched off. These are independent outstanding jobs; neither is finished until the corresponding action occurs.
u30: Prepared food still needs serving, a taken order still needs preparation, and a client is waiting to order. The siren is ringing, so its switch must also be toggled off. These are all open requirements, and none of them is finished yet.
u31: Prepared food awaits service, a taken order awaits preparation, and a client is waiting to give their order. Food has just fallen and must be picked up on the next step, or the task fails irreversibly. If the pickup succeeds, the prepared-food, order-preparation, and waiting-client obligations all remain.
u32: Prepared food still needs serving, a taken order still needs preparation, a client is waiting to order, and the siren is ringing. Food has also just slipped and must be picked up on the very next step to avoid irreversible failure. After that pickup, the siren switch, the prepared portion, the taken order, and the waiting client all still require attention.
u4: Food has been prepared for a waiting client's taken order. The remaining step for this client is to serve the prepared food. Until the food is handed over, the order is not complete.
u5: Prepared food is ready for a waiting client, and the siren is sounding. The food still needs to be served, and the siren switch still needs to be toggled. Both jobs remain open until those actions occur.
u6: The food has just slipped out of the agent's hands, and no other order or ringing obligation is active. The very next step must leave the agent holding food again by picking it up; if it does not, the mandatory immediate-recovery rule is broken. After a successful recovery, the shop returns to waiting for the next event.
u7: The food has just slipped while the siren is ringing. The next step must recover the food so the agent is holding it again; failing that immediate pickup would break a hard rule. Once the food is back in hand, the siren still has to be switched off.
u8: A client's order has been taken and the food has just slipped. The next step must put food back in the agent's hands; after that, the waiting order still needs the food prepared at the stove and served. The slip makes the pickup urgent, but it does not cancel the client's order.
u9: A taken order is waiting and the siren is ringing just as the food has slipped. The very next step must recover the food by holding it again, or the immediate-recovery requirement fails. Afterwards, the order still needs preparation and serving, and the siren must be switched off.
